meta.name: Agent incident tracker
meta.rule: Only incidents with an official source: the vendor's disclosure, a security advisory, or a named researcher's report marked as such.

incidents.title: Binance said its initial investigation suggests an attacker used a compromised DevOps engineer's laptop to reach a service container and submit unauthorized withdrawal transactions, and that it found no evidence of a wallet private key compromise. It suspended all deposits and withdrawals as a precaution, is working with law enforcement, says it will cover all losses and will publish a full post-mortem once the investigation is complete.

Polymarket said one of its third-party providers was compromised, affecting users of its international platform Polymarket.com; it put the exchange in cancel-only mode, paused relayer actions and halted trading for about an hour (18:05-19:05 UTC, Trading API included), fixed the issue, referred it to law enforcement and says anyone impacted will be made whole.

Predict.fun said a small number of users had unauthorized transfers from their wallets totaling about 400,000 USDT. Its preliminary investigation points to its API documentation site, hosted by a third-party provider, being compromised; the docs site is offline until the investigation ends. Predict.fun says it will fully reimburse affected users and publish a post-mortem.

Coinbase said a security incident at its third-party analytics vendor Amplitude exposed contact information for a 'small subset' of customers. It said its systems showed no unauthorized access and customer funds remain safe.

Bloom said an attacker exploited a remote code execution vulnerability in a third-party module and drained 49 wallet addresses belonging to 9 users, about 9,408 SOL ($947,000); it says no private keys were compromised and took all systems offline as a precaution. Later the same day Bloom said all 9,408 SOL had been refunded to the 9 users. No detailed post-mortem yet.

Keystone's full statement: an attacker used a vulnerability in a third-party monitoring tool on its website (detected October 20) to take 25,964 buyer records, 12,873 unpaid checkout records and the WebAuth key used to check that a device is genuine. Keystone says recovery phrases and private keys were not involved; the risk is counterfeit devices passing the authenticity check. It is destroying 18,835 inventory devices with the old key and asks anyone who received a device after October 20 to follow its verification guidance.

Foundation (Passport hardware wallet) said phishing emails were sent from its own domains after attackers got into part of its backend through a vulnerability in a self-hosted application and likely accessed its customer support inbox; some emails included customers' mailing addresses or phone numbers. Foundation says Passport devices and funds are not compromised, it cut off the attackers' email access within about 10 minutes and revoked all API keys. Never enter seed words anywhere except on the Passport itself.

Initia said a bug in MoveVM script caching let an attacker credit themselves unbacked WETH, iUSD and USDC and bridge about $2.7M out (via LayerZero and CCTP, swapped to 1,135.52 ETH) before it halted the L1 and its rollups; it said no native INIT was minted and that a fix was being written and audited.

Keystone said a third party pulled customer shipping data (names, contact details, shipping addresses, items bought and prices) from its website store via the Shopify API, detected October 20 and confirmed October 23; it said payment details, recovery phrases, private keys and wallet passwords were not exposed, and warned of scammers posing as Keystone with refunds or replacement devices.

Electrum released 4.8.3 as a security update; press reports of its advisory say earlier versions let a malicious Electrum server plant a fake pending payment so that a later fee bump (RBF) paid the attacker, and that users of trusted servers were not exposed. Update to 4.8.3 or later.

GMO Internet shut down its Onamae.com Desktop Cloud Windows VPS service (popular for running FX trading bots on MT4/MT5) after finding programs planted by a third party on customer servers on October 20; up to 26,739 servers may be affected, customers reported unauthorized trades from trading logins stored on the servers, and GMO says it refused a ransom demand. It is paying every customer ¥5,000 and will compensate confirmed losses from unauthorized trades. From a device you don't trade on, change your broker and platform passwords, end sessions and turn on 2FA.

Railway disclosed that an unauthorized third party may have accessed encrypted environment variables and obtained the decrypted contents of some of them; it told users to immediately roll all environment variables and API keys stored in Railway and paused all deployments while it investigates.

Microsoft reported that the China-state aligned actor Storm-0940 used ARTEX, an open-source multi-agent LLM penetration-testing framework, to automate scanning, password spraying and OAuth app abuse in a ConnectWise cloud backup supply-chain compromise aimed at hundreds of organizations.

Node.js security releases v22.23.4, v24.22.1 and v26.12.1 fix ten vulnerabilities, including a high-severity Brotli decoder out-of-bounds write that permits remote code execution (CVE-2026-111497) in the 22.x, 24.x and 26.x lines.

Qubic said an attacker drained 1,404 Qubic wallets (about 2.94 trillion QU) between 23:42 UTC on October 17 and 01:26 UTC on October 18 because some wallet seeds were generated with insufficient randomness (seeds made on iPhone or iPad browsers or Mac Safari before October 18, 2026, or in the Qubic iOS app before July 2025); it says the protocol itself was not at fault. Computors halted the network; on October 20 Qubic said the recovery was approved and opened a reclaim platform (weak-seed-reclaim.qubic.org, claims until May 1, 2027).

Ledger said hardware wallets sold through the Southeast Asian reseller CryptoBilis contained hidden implants that read the screen during setup, captured the 24-word recovery phrase and sent it out over LTE through an embedded eSIM; attackers then drained funds (drains on October 9, disclosed October 13). Ledger says the implant leaves the Secure Element intact, so tampered devices may still pass its authenticity check, and that all confirmed thefts involve CryptoBilis devices.

MetaMask said it was responding to a security incident in part of its infrastructure, in its non-custodial staking operations, and exited affected Ethereum staking validators (including its Lido validators) as a precaution. It said it found no immediate threat to MetaMask wallets and did not disclose the cause.

An intruder at Brevo, Trezor's newsletter provider, exported 347,149 marketing email contacts and sent Trezor subscribers a fake 'STM32 entropy vulnerability' email asking for wallet backups. Trezor said no Trezor product, wallet or account system was affected.
